meta.title: 年薪50万不是5份10万｜两个杠杆

scenes.context: 讲者回忆新天地西班牙餐厅的肉疼经历，引出老板的杠杆理论。
sentences: 你说年薪50万的工作，是不是干了5份年薪10万的工作？
A 500k-a-year job—is it really just five 100k jobs stacked together?
年薪：annual salary；干5份：do five of them
当年我年薪刚过10万、非常缺钱的时候，好不容易约了个漂亮的妹子周末逛街，逛到新天地一家西班牙餐厅，打开菜单一看——哎呦，那个价格，现在想想都肉疼。

Back when I'd just crossed the 100k mark and money was tight, I finally scored a date with a cute girl. We strolled into a Spanish restaurant in Xintiandi—and when I opened the menu and saw the paella prices, it stung just thinking about it.
新天地：Xintiandi (上海地标)；肉疼：it stings, it still hurts
后来我向当时的老板讨教，他告诉我：年薪50万，绝对不是年薪10万的工作做5份。
Later I picked my then-boss's brain about this, and he told me: a 500k salary is by no means five 100k jobs.
讨教：pick someone's brain；绝不是：by no means
paraphrase: 没钱时的窘境 → 被菜单价格刺痛
Being broke → getting stung by the menu prices.
疑问「50万是5份10万？」 → 老板给出答案
Wondering if 500k is five 100ks → the boss sets him straight.
scenes.speak: A 500k-a-year job—is it really just five 100k jobs stacked together? Back when I'd just crossed the 100k mark and money was tight, I finally scored a date with a cute girl. We strolled into a Spanish restaurant in Xintiandi, and when I opened the menu and saw the paella prices, it stung just thinking about it. Later I picked my then-boss's brain about this, and he told me: a 500k salary is by no means five 100k jobs.

scenes.title_en: Lever one: break the role ceiling
scenes.context: 讲者讲把上下游岗位的活装进自己脑袋，就能指挥更多人。
sentences: 从20万到50万，你的工作需要加两个杠杆。第一个杠杆，突破岗位限制。
To go from 200k to 500k, you need to add two levers to your job. The first lever: break the ceiling of your role.
杠杆：leverage / lever；突破岗位限制：break the role ceiling
如果只做好手边的工作，那你只是一个优秀的螺丝钉；但只要你愿意，你可以把齿轮、钻头、电动机的活，全部装进自己的脑袋里。
If you only do the work right in front of you, you're just a great cog. But if you're willing, you can cram the jobs of the gear, the drill, and the motor all into your own head.
螺丝钉：cog in the machine；装进脑袋：cram … into your head
一个流程假定有6个步骤，你只负责其中一个步骤；同时你还能指挥好其他5个人，那很好，说明你有可能做这6个人的领导了。
Say a process has six steps and you're responsible for just one. If you can also direct the other five people well, that's great—you just might become the leader of all six.
指挥：direct / orchestrate；做6个人的领导：become the leader of all six
paraphrase: 只做手边活 → 优秀的螺丝钉
Doing only your own task → being a great cog.
把上下游的活装进脑袋 → 能指挥更多人
Absorbing others' roles → being able to direct more people.
scenes.speak: To go from 200k to 500k, you need to add two levers to your job. The first lever: break the ceiling of your role. If you only do the work right in front of you, you're just a great cog. But if you're willing, you can cram the jobs of the gear, the drill, and the motor all into your own head. Say a process has six steps and you're responsible for just one. If you can also direct the other five people well, that's great—you just might become the leader of all six.

scenes.title_en: Lever two: break the skill ceiling
scenes.context: 讲者讲经理总监级技能让年薪乘2乘3，并用自己的实践验证。
sentences: 第二个杠杆，是突破技能限制。如果只会销售技能，做得再好，也只能是带两三个人的主管；但要做到经理、总监级别，需要财务、战略、公关、演讲、协作、培训等等技能。

The second lever is breaking the skill ceiling. If sales is your only skill, you'll top out as a supervisor with two or three people no matter how good you are. But manager and director level requires finance, strategy, PR, public speaking, collaboration, training, and so on.
突破技能限制：break the skill ceiling；总监：director；公关：public relations (PR)
你的本职岗位工作年薪是10万，但你的其他技能，可以让你的年薪乘以2、乘以3。因为公司要用你这个技能，就不必再花钱另外请个人，对公司来说还是省钱的。

Your core role pays 100k a year, but your other skills can multiply that by two or three. Because if the company can put your skills to work, it doesn't have to hire and pay someone extra—which still saves money.
本职岗位：core role；乘以2乘以3：multiply by two or three；省钱：save money
你看到这条视频就是个例子——写、拍、剪都是我一个人干的。储备技能、一专多能，确实像杠杆一样撬动年薪，同时劳动时间并没有增加。本人亲测管用，推荐给你。

This very video is the proof—writing, filming, editing, all done by me alone. Stocking up on skills and being good at many things really levers up your salary, and your working hours don't grow. I've tried it myself and it works. Give it a shot.
写拍剪：write, film and edit；一专多能：one specialty, many skills；撬动：lever up；亲测：tried and tested
paraphrase: 技能单一 → 年薪封顶
A single skill → a capped salary.
技能多样 → 年薪乘2乘3
Multiple skills → a salary multiplied by two or three.
scenes.speak: The second lever is breaking the skill ceiling. If sales is your only skill, you'll top out as a supervisor with two or three people no matter how good you are. But manager and director level requires finance, strategy, PR, public speaking, collaboration, training, and so on. Your core role pays 100k a year, but your other skills can multiply that by two or three. Because if the company can put your skills to work, it doesn't have to hire and pay someone extra—which still saves money. This very video is the proof—writing, filming, editing, all done by me alone. Stocking up on skills and being good at many things really levers up your salary, and your working hours don't grow. I've tried it myself and it works. Give it a shot.

practice: She earns 500k a year—an annual salary of half a million.
It's not five 100k jobs stacked together.
Your extra skills act as leverage on your salary.
It still hurts to think about that price.
pitfalls: ✕ 直译腔：Is the 500k job doing 5 of the 100k jobs?
✓ 地道说法：Is a 500k job just five 100k jobs rolled into one?
「干5份」别直译 do five jobs，用 rolled into one / stacked together 更自然。
✕ 直译腔：The price makes my flesh hurt.
✓ 地道说法：The price stings. / It still hurts to think about it.
肉疼 是口语夸张，英文用 sting / hurt，不逐字直译。
✕ 直译腔：My skills can multiply my salary times 2 times 3.
✓ 地道说法：My skills can multiply my salary by two or even three.
「乘以2乘以3」→ multiply by two and by three，别写 times 2 times 3。
✕ 直译腔：You are just an excellent screw.
✓ 地道说法：You're just a cog in the machine.
螺丝钉 的比喻对应 cog in the machine，而不是物理上的 screw。
shifts: 以为「年薪50万」= 多干5份10万的活
明白「年薪50万」= 工作带杠杆
只守着岗位上的手边活
把上下游岗位的活装进自己脑袋
主动储备一专多能的可迁移技能
footer_notes: ASR 专有名词已按语境校正（如「主本」→「主管」、「恶劣」→「历练」、「一串多能」→「一专多能」、「清澈管用」→「亲测管用」）。场景/句子朗读使用 edge-tts，单词发音使用浏览器 Web Speech API。
